video_title: Why The AI Bubble Isn’t Dot-Com 2.0 with David Steinberg, Zeta Global Founder & CEO
gist: Zeta Global CEO David Steinberg (quiet period, so no quarter talk) makes the case for Zeta: 30%+ revenue CAGR to about $1.8B, a rule of 67, NRR above 120%, and still a 70% multiple discount to peers. He outlines Athena OS, a custom inference chip and the Palantir Foundry partnership. He argues the AI boom differs from dot-com because the public spenders are hugely profitable, and that bubble risk sits in private AI startups.

insights.claim: Zeta Global re-architected its entire platform starting in 2017, forgoing roughly $50M+ of annual EBITDA for several years and dedicating 400 full-time engineers to make data and AI core to the application layer, rolling it out in 2020.
insights.speaker: David Steinberg (Zeta Global CEO)
insights.so_what: Early AI-native re-architecture is Steinberg's explanation for Zeta's growth since ChatGPT made AI a boardroom topic.
insights.quote: we were going to take 400 full-time engineers and re-architect into what they thought was science fiction

insights.claim: Zeta Global did about $283M trailing revenue at its June 2021 IPO and expects just over $1.8B revenue this year at the middle of its range, a 4-year ~30%+ revenue CAGR with ~50% compounded EBITDA growth and ~75% compounded free cash flow growth.
insights.speaker: David Steinberg (Zeta Global CEO)
insights.so_what: Revenue has grown roughly 6x since the IPO, with profit compounding faster than sales.
insights.quote: This year at the middle of our range we'll do just over 1.8 billion in revenue.

insights.claim: Zeta Global's most recent quarter showed 44% top-line growth, 53% EBITDA growth and 73% free cash flow growth, and Steinberg says profit has more than doubled in the last 18 months.
insights.speaker: David Steinberg (Zeta Global CEO)
insights.so_what: Growth is accelerating, not decelerating, at $1.8B scale.
insights.quote: Last quarter, we grew the business 44% top line, 53% EBITDA, and 73% free cash flow growth.

insights.claim: Zeta Global has beaten and raised guidance in all 20 quarters it has reported as a public company.
insights.speaker: David Steinberg (Zeta Global CEO)
insights.so_what: A consistent beat-and-raise record supports management's credibility on guidance.
insights.quote: We've beat our guidance and raised our guidance 20 quarters in a row.

insights.claim: Steinberg cites an independent Forrester survey finding Zeta clients earn a 600-700% return on marketing spend versus about 200% for average competitors, and his long-term goal is 1,000%.
insights.speaker: David Steinberg (Zeta Global CEO)
insights.so_what: ROI gap is the core of Zeta's competitive moat argument as buyers demand AI ROI.

insights.claim: Steinberg says Zeta trades at a 70% multiple discount to its peer cohort (Palantir, Snowflake, CrowdStrike, MongoDB and others), and at a lower multiple than when its stock was half today's price.
insights.speaker: David Steinberg (Zeta Global CEO)
insights.so_what: Management frames ZETA as a re-rating candidate if the multiple gap narrows.
insights.quote: We trade today at a 70% multiple discount to our compatibles.

insights.claim: Zeta reports net revenue retention above 120% last year and a 'rule of 67' last quarter; within its 7-9 company cohort only Palantir scores higher on both, and Zeta ranked number one of nine on free cash flow to market cap at 5%.
insights.speaker: David Steinberg (Zeta Global CEO)
insights.so_what: Zeta's KPIs are top-tier inside its peer group even though its multiple is not.

insights.claim: Steinberg attributes Zeta's valuation discount to a negative market perception of marketing spend as the first budget cut in a downturn, noting Zeta grew double digits during COVID.
insights.speaker: David Steinberg (Zeta Global CEO)
insights.so_what: If the 'marketing is cyclical' discount fades as Zeta diversifies beyond marketing, the multiple could close the gap.

insights.claim: Dan Nathan argues Palantir's valuation is unprecedented: about a half-trillion-dollar market cap against perhaps $20B in sales next year on a generous estimate, versus an LTM of about $8B last quarter, though Steinberg counters that it is doubling with extraordinary FCF growth.
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan (host)
insights.so_what: Even bulls on the business disagree on whether PLTR's price is justified.
insights.quote: It's a half a trillion dollar market cap company that might do I'm just going to be really generous. Let's say $20 billion in sales next year.

themes.theme: Athena OS, chips and product expansion

insights.claim: Zeta is expanding from marketing into enterprise intelligence: Athena OS uses its data cloud and AI for logistics, supply chain, finance, cyber protection and fraud detection, after clients ran out of inventory from Zeta-driven demand and asked for help with inventory management.
insights.speaker: David Steinberg (Zeta Global CEO)
insights.so_what: Expanding beyond marketing grows Zeta's addressable market and could reduce the discount for being a 'marketing' stock.
insights.quote: And Athena OS is the future of our company.

insights.claim: Zeta made its Athena voice agent headless via MCP and says it is already integrated into ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini.
insights.speaker: David Steinberg (Zeta Global CEO)
insights.so_what: Zeta is distributing its agent through the frontier assistants instead of competing with them.
insights.quote: She's MCP now.

insights.claim: Zeta announced a custom inference chip with a low-capital structure: a manufacturing partner builds and pays for it, a hosting partner buys it, and Zeta gets exclusive on-demand access.
insights.speaker: David Steinberg (Zeta Global CEO)
insights.so_what: Zeta gets custom silicon without heavy capex on its balance sheet.
insights.quote: We have a manufacturing partner who's going to make them and they're going to pay for it.

insights.claim: Zeta re-architected its data cloud on Palantir Foundry, which Steinberg says made millisecond decisioning even faster, and through the Palantir relationship Zeta has been added to FedRAMP for government contracts ('Zeta Gov').
insights.speaker: David Steinberg (Zeta Global CEO)
insights.so_what: The Palantir partnership opens a government revenue channel for Zeta.

insights.claim: Zeta's data cloud covers over 550M opted-in individuals globally (240M+ in the US) with 5,000-7,000 data elements per person, ingesting signals from 5.2M publishers plus most US credit card transactions monthly, and never sells data or exposes PII to clients.
insights.speaker: David Steinberg (Zeta Global CEO)
insights.so_what: Proprietary consented data is the asset that frontier models cannot copy.

insights.claim: Steinberg says Zeta Live returned about $10 of business per $1 spent last year and he expects 12-14x this year; attendance reached 3,700 at Lincoln Center against a 2,000 target.
insights.speaker: David Steinberg (Zeta Global CEO)
insights.so_what: Client events are a measurable sales channel for Zeta, not just marketing spend.

themes.theme: AI architecture: data sovereignty and app-layer winners

insights.claim: Steinberg splits AI-era software into two camps: enterprises that make AI core to the application layer through re-architecture and proprietary data, and 'workflow management tools' that only deliver cost efficiency and will see customers migrate to intelligent infrastructure.
insights.speaker: David Steinberg (Zeta Global CEO)
insights.so_what: A way to tell durable AI-era software winners from SaaS likely to be disrupted.
insights.quote: They were created to effectively disintermediate large numbers of employees, but they don't create intelligence.

insights.claim: Steinberg argues any enterprise giving its data to a foundation model is giving away its business; Zeta has never exposed its data cloud to a frontier model and runs its own AI built on open-source tools.
insights.speaker: David Steinberg (Zeta Global CEO)
insights.so_what: Data sovereignty favors vendors that keep proprietary data out of frontier labs.
insights.quote: any enterprise that's giving their data to a foundation model is giving away their business

insights.claim: Steinberg argues inference for targeting needs small datasets rather than the whole internet, so specialized inference models can beat frontier models on enterprise tasks like credit-card propensity scoring.
insights.speaker: David Steinberg (Zeta Global CEO)
insights.so_what: Inference economics favor vertical models built on proprietary data.
insights.quote: I'm not writing a poem.

insights.claim: Steinberg cites Jensen Huang saying 75% of the economics of the AI revolution will accrue to the application layer, and positions Zeta as an application-layer winner, as in the internet build.
insights.speaker: David Steinberg (Zeta Global CEO)
insights.so_what: The app layer's share of AI economics is Zeta's main bull argument.
insights.quote: 75% of the economics of the AI revolution are going to be in the application layer

themes.theme: Agentic internet and frontier lab landscape

insights.claim: Steinberg predicts two internets: an agentic internet and the HTTP layer; Zeta's acquisition of Sense of AI targets agentic commerce and generative engine optimization (informing frontier models about products relevant to user queries).
insights.speaker: David Steinberg (Zeta Global CEO)
insights.so_what: Generative engine optimization (GEO) could replace SEO as a marketing budget line.
insights.quote: There's going to be the agentic internet and then there's going to be the HTTP layer.

insights.claim: Steinberg says Meta's Muse personalization agent hit about 10 million downloads in a week, perhaps second only to ChatGPT, while Nathan notes uptake was underwhelming relative to Meta's one-third-of-the-planet user base and the stock's narrative turned after earnings.
insights.speaker: David Steinberg (Zeta Global CEO)
insights.so_what: Early Muse adoption data is contested; it is a key test of whether Meta's AI spend pays off.
insights.quote: 10 million downloads in a week

insights.claim: Steinberg views OpenAI as the clear consumer leader, with an advertising business growing faster than Zeta expected, while Anthropic is moving more into coding/enterprise and trades leadership on model quality with Gemini.
insights.speaker: David Steinberg (Zeta Global CEO)
insights.so_what: The frontier labs are splitting by segment rather than one winner taking all.
insights.quote: they're the clear leader in consumer

insights.claim: Steinberg expects both closed frontier models and open-source/open-weight models to win, noting open source requires heavy customization labor, citing IBM's Red Hat acquisition.
insights.speaker: David Steinberg (Zeta Global CEO)
insights.so_what: Open-weight pressure on frontier pricing may be limited by integration costs.
insights.quote: I think they're both going to win.

insights.claim: Steinberg says distribution decides AI winners (as it did for Walmart, JPMorgan Chase and Google), so Google, Elon Musk's X/Grok and Meta are structural winners, and he calls Elon the single biggest competitive advantage in business.
insights.speaker: David Steinberg (Zeta Global CEO)
insights.so_what: Incumbents with distribution and data have the edge in the AI race.
insights.quote: distribution is why Walmart wins

insights.claim: The hosts note Anthropic's S-1 dropped the day of recording with an IPO expected within weeks, and OpenAI has suggested listing around Q1/early Q2 2027; Steinberg says a lot will hang on how Anthropic does.
insights.speaker: David Steinberg (Zeta Global CEO)
insights.so_what: Anthropic's IPO reception is a key sentiment catalyst for AI and software stocks.
insights.quote: a lot is going to hang on how Anthropic does

insights.claim: Steinberg argues today's AI capex is different from the dot-com bubble because the public spenders are so profitable that, if they stopped, they could cover debt service and some could repay the debt within about a year, unlike cash-burning dot-com public companies.
insights.speaker: David Steinberg (Zeta Global CEO)
insights.so_what: Hyperscaler balance-sheet strength lowers systemic bubble risk among public companies.
insights.quote: some of them could repay it in like a year

insights.claim: Steinberg flags well-funded private AI companies other than OpenAI and Anthropic, which he sees as 'more products than businesses', as the real risk, doubting they can ever justify the capital raised at those valuations.
insights.speaker: David Steinberg (Zeta Global CEO)
insights.so_what: Bubble risk is concentrated in private AI valuations, not public megacaps.
insights.quote: build businesses that are probably more products than businesses

insights.claim: Steinberg draws a parallel to Quest Communications's overbuilt dark fiber, made useful by unforeseen compression technology, and expects a similar efficiency breakthrough for data centers over the next 10-20 years.
insights.speaker: David Steinberg (Zeta Global CEO)
insights.so_what: Efficiency breakthroughs could strand or repurpose today's data center capacity, as they did with fiber.

insights.claim: Nathan notes that in summer 2023, software stocks like Salesforce, Adobe, Workday and ServiceNow were seen as AI's biggest beneficiaries, then sold off about 70% before coming back, showing how fast narratives change.
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan (host)
insights.so_what: Software sentiment swings are violent, so positioning around them should be cautious.
insights.quote: narratives change quickly
